shorts.title: Obama's Library: "Approximately $1 Billion" And Counting #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, the Obama Foundation just told Fox News Digital that its Chicago presidential center will cost, quote, "approximately $1 billion." [beat] The first estimate? As low as three hundred million dollars. [sarcastic] That's not a budget, friends, that's a teaser trailer. The next most expensive presidential library is George W. Bush's, at three hundred twenty-seven million. [beat] Obama's is triple that. The foundation says it's all private money, and the lawsuits over Jackson Park slowed things down, fair enough. [amused] But I notice the party that lectures us about affordability can't build a library without a few zeros sneaking in. Luke fourteen, in the King James: "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?" [beat] Somebody forgot to count, folks. Now tell me in the comments: would you let your contractor triple the bill? Subscribe, Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: The Obama Foundation projects the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago will cost about $1 billion, which would make it the costliest U.S. presidential center; foundation spokeswoman Emily Bittner said the total cost is "approximately $1 billion."
Initial estimates were as low as $300 million.
The George W. Bush Presidential Library, at $327 million, is the next most expensive.
The foundation says the funding was all raised in private contributions; delays included a court battle with residents and the park's National Register listing.

shorts.title: Musk: Ukraine Limits Set By "The US Military And Ultimately POTUS" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Musk Points Finger At The President
shorts.narration: [serious] Ukraine woke up to a surprise. Starshield, the military version of SpaceX's satellite service, got speed limits overnight. One Ukrainian drone unit cancelled missions. [beat] So who did it? Elon Musk posted, quote, "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS." [deadpan] Translation, friends: not me, talk to the boss. Fox says he didn't say who signed off, and nobody has confirmed he ordered it. [beat] Senator Thom Tillis, a Republican, asked SpaceX to confirm that wasn't its intent. [serious] And Poland's foreign minister asked Musk if he was playing politics with his products again. Psalm one forty-six, verse three, King James: "Put not your trust in princes." [beat] Or in billionaires with a keyboard. Who should answer for this, Musk or the Pentagon? Tell me below. Subscribe for the daily news.

claims.text: Ukraine lost access to SpaceX's Starshield service after new speed-related restrictions took effect overnight; the U.S. government owns and controls the Starshield satellites and infrastructure.
Elon Musk posted on X: "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Musk did not say whether Trump, Hegseth or another official authorized the restriction; no public confirmation has emerged that Musk personally ordered it.
A Ukrainian drone unit on the Huliaipole front cancelled missions due to connectivity problems.
Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., asked SpaceX, "Can you confirm that's not SpaceX's intent?"; Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski asked Musk, "are you playing politics with your products again?"

slides.text: Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.
slides.speaker: Elon Musk

shorts.title: Hinson To Dem Turek In Iowa Debate: "42% Of The Time" #Shorts
shorts.hook: "42% Of The Time Is All He Showed Up"
shorts.narration: [mischievously] The Iowa Senate debate gave us a scorecard. Republican Ashley Hinson told Democrat Josh Turek, quote, "42% of the time is all Rep. Turek showed up to work this year." [beat] Fox News reports Turek missed 261 votes in the Iowa legislature between January and May. His defense? "I'm out campaigning." [deadpan] So he's too busy applying for the job to do the job. [beat] To be fair, Turek fired back that Hinson missed 193 votes. Her campaign says that's across her entire congressional career. [amused] Folks, one of these numbers is a year and one is a decade. Proverbs fourteen, twenty-three, King James: "In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury." [beat] Showing up is half of life, and 42 percent is a failing grade in any school. Is campaigning a valid excuse for skipping votes? Sound off below. Subscribe, Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: At the Oct. 13, 2026 televised debate in Des Moines, Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson said: "42% of the time is all Rep. Turek showed up to work this year."
Fox News Digital reported Turek missed 261 votes in the Iowa legislature from Jan. 12 to May 3, 2026, about 58% of votes in that period.
Turek said: "I'm out campaigning. I'm out meeting Iowans all over all 99 counties." and "She also missed 193 votes."
Hinson's campaign said her 193 missed votes covered her entire congressional career, while Turek's 261 were from the 2026 legislative session alone.
